rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the eight-compound elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing retained compounds. Use a midrange temperature so subsequent runs can probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Keep the gradient fixed and raise temperature to test selectivity for the only unresolved pair, R = 0.72. The higher temperature should also shorten retention, preserving room to use a shallower gradient if needed.

Slightly reduce gradient steepness at the best temperature to try to lift the early pair from R = 1.41 above 1.5. The last peak at 6.56 minutes leaves ample room for this change without a time penalty.

The maximum CRF is already achieved; now test a shorter fully resolved method. This gradient slope lies between injections 2 and 3, aiming to retain R ≥ 1.5 for the early pair while bringing the last peak forward.

Trim the gradient window and raise the starting organic fraction slightly, keeping the slope close to the fully resolved injection 4. This tests whether retention can be shortened while preserving separation of the early critical pair.

Restore the lower starting organic fraction that preserved the early pair, and use a slightly steeper slope than injection 4 to shorten retention. The final organic fraction remains above the estimated last-peak elution composition, so all peaks should remain within the gradient.

Test a slightly steeper gradient near the early pair’s resolution limit while retaining the low starting organic fraction. The last peak may move into the final hold, so this run will determine whether the shorter gradient actually reduces its elution time.

Test whether a shallower slope restores full resolution at the higher starting organic fraction used in injection 5. This probes an alternative window for balancing early-pair separation against total retention time, while keeping the maximum-score methods in reserve.

Test a small increase in slope beyond injection 7 to locate the shortest fully resolved boundary, with a higher endpoint to avoid a final-hold delay. The early pair is close to R = 1.5, so this is a boundary test; injection 7 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Probe the untested low-temperature endpoint for an alternative selectivity regime, since the 60 °C slope boundary is now well bracketed. This broad gradient limits late-elution risk while testing whether a change in elution order could resolve the critical pair.

Test whether modest warming separates the late cluster seen at 25 °C while retaining adequate early-pair selectivity. The shorter gradient also probes whether this lower-temperature regime can compete with the fastest fully resolved method.

Test a higher starting organic fraction at an intermediate temperature to seek a different selectivity balance for the early pair and late cluster. Warming from 30 °C should spread the late cluster, while the higher start should shorten retention.

Reduce the slope from injection 12 to improve the early pair’s R = 1.17 while preserving the resolved late cluster. This tests a second fully resolved temperature regime, with the last peak expected to remain below 10 minutes.

Return to the maximum-score temperature and test a shallower gradient for greater resolution margin than the near-threshold fast methods. Relative to injection 8, this should strengthen the early pair while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Raise the gradient window by 0.05 while preserving injection 14’s slope to shorten retention. Its early-pair resolution margin provides room to test whether the higher starting composition can retain full separation.

Test a narrower, shallower gradient at 30 °C to spread the late cluster that limited injection 11. The higher starting organic fraction offsets some of the added retention, while probing whether the early pair remains resolved in this alternative selectivity regime.

Slightly flatten injection 13’s gradient to lift its sole unresolved pair from R = 1.39 toward full resolution. The last peak is expected to remain below 10 minutes, potentially establishing another maximum-score method at a lower temperature.

Refine the higher-starting-organic branch with a slope just steeper than injection 8, aiming to retain R ≥ 1.5 while shortening last-peak retention. Injection 7 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test whether shifting injection 13’s window upward at the same slope improves early-pair selectivity while shortening retention. The late cluster was already resolved at this temperature and slope, making the early pair the main uncertainty.

With the fastest resolved boundary bracketed, test a shallower gradient at the low starting composition for a larger resolution margin. This should retain the maximum CRF with the last peak below 10 minutes, providing a less borderline alternative to injection 7.

Shorten injection 20’s gradient and trim its endpoint, increasing the slope slightly to bring the last peak forward. The two limiting pairs both have resolution margin near R = 2, so this should preserve full resolution while reducing time.

Raise injection 21’s endpoint one grid step to shorten retention while retaining some early-pair resolution margin. This intermediate slope should preserve the maximum CRF and offer a faster alternative to the methods with minimum R near 2.

Increase the endpoint one more step to shorten retention while targeting full resolution. This matches injection 3’s successful slope with a shorter programmed gradient and an endpoint above the estimated last-peak elution composition.

Trim the higher-starting-organic method to an eight-minute gradient with a slightly shallower slope than injection 18. This should preserve full resolution with more margin than its R = 1.50 critical pair, while keeping all peaks within the gradient.

Test a six-minute gradient with injection 23’s fully resolved slope, targeting more resolution margin than injection 7 at the same programmed duration. The last peak will elute during the hold, but should remain below 10 minutes and preserve the maximum CRF.
